pr.title: Add focus follows mouse accessibility setting
pr.body:
Implements an initial focus-follows-mouse behavior for https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/93772 (per-terminal handling intentionally deferred; see discussion), as agreed with @meganrogge in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/93772#issuecomment-4466612536.

## What this does

When enabled, hovering a workbench part moves keyboard focus to it after a short debounce, so the keyboard goes where the mouse is rather than where you last clicked.

- Side Bar, Panel, and Auxiliary Bar via `IWorkbenchLayoutService.focusPart`
- Editor groups via `group.focus()` (groups added/removed at runtime are tracked)

## Settings

- `accessibility.focusFollowsMouse.enabled` (boolean, default `false`)
- `accessibility.focusFollowsMouse.delay` (number ms, default `200`, minimum `0`)

## Design notes

- Implemented as an `IWorkbenchContribution` registered at `AfterRestored`, following the sibling `UnfocusedViewDimmingContribution` and the `accessibility.dimUnfocused.*` settings conventions.
- Debounced (default 200ms) so brief mouse transit does not steal focus; the delay is read live so changes apply without reload.
- Guards: no focus shift while a mouse button is held (drag/selection), or while a context menu is open; a `mouseleave` cancels a still-pending focus.
- Part listeners are main-window only; editor groups are covered across windows via `IEditorGroupsService`. Per-terminal handling is intentionally out of scope for this initial version.

## How to test

1. Set `"accessibility.focusFollowsMouse.enabled": true`.
2. Move the mouse (without clicking) over the editor, a split editor group, the Side Bar, or the Panel/terminal; after ~200ms the keyboard focus follows. Typing then goes to the hovered part.
3. Adjust `accessibility.focusFollowsMouse.delay` and confirm the timing changes.
4. Confirm focus does not shift while dragging a selection or with a context menu open.
5. Toggle the setting off and confirm the behavior stops.

## Testing done

- Unit tests added (14, covering enable/disable, runtime toggle, the guards, group lifecycle, and the configurable delay).
- Manually verified the full behavior (including the control and guards) in a development build with real mouse and keyboard input on Linux.
- ESLint, hygiene, and layer checks pass for the changed files.

Note: manual verification was on Linux; the change is platform-agnostic browser-layer code (standard DOM mouse events plus core workbench services, no OS-specific APIs), so it is expected to behave the same on Windows, macOS, web, and remote, but I have not personally tested those targets.

I will sign the CLA when the bot prompts.

- feat(accessibility): add configurable accessibility.focusFollowsMouse.delay setting (default 200ms)
- feat(accessibility): add FocusFollowsMouseContribution
- feat(accessibility): register contribution at Restored lifecycle phase
- test(accessibility): add FocusFollowsMouseContribution unit tests
